profile.summary: AlphaFold-Multimer predicts the structure of a protein complex. It is the multi-chain mode of AlphaFold v2: the input is a FASTA file holding every chain of the complex, alignments are built against several sequence databases, and the system returns coordinates together with per-residue and per-pair confidence estimates, pTM and predicted aligned error. Five trained parameter sets are shipped, and by default each is run with five random seeds, giving 25 predictions that are ranked. It is the same code base as single chain AlphaFold, selected with one flag, and the developers call the multimer implementation a work in progress that is less stable than the monomer system.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: The pipeline has two halves. First a data pipeline searches genetic databases to build alignments and find templates: BFD, MGnify, PDB70, the PDB in mmCIF format, UniRef30, UniRef90, and for the multimer mode also PDB seqres and UniProt. Then the neural network predicts the structure, and the multimer models carry heads for a distogram, masked MSA, experimentally resolved atoms, predicted aligned error and predicted lDDT. The current weights come from the v2.3.0 update: the same architecture and training method as the AlphaFold-Multimer paper, fine tuned on PDB structures up to 2021-09-30 instead of 2018-04-30, with the training crop raised from 384 to 640 residues, the number of chains used at training raised from 8 to 20, and the maximum number of alignment sequences raised from 1,152 to 2,048 for three of the five models. The self-distillation set was also rebuilt from clustered MGnify with a looser cluster filter.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The default multimer preset names five models, model_1_multimer_v3 through model_5_multimer_v3, and the parameter file for them is alphafold_params_2022-12-06.tar. Two older generations remain usable but deprecated: the v2.2.0 weights from alphafold_params_2022-03-02.tar, selected by changing _v3 to _v2 in the multimer presets, and the v2.1.0 weights from alphafold_params_2022-01-19.tar, selected by removing _v3. The code applies version-specific differences to the configuration, mostly for numerical stability. Reproducibility also depends on the database snapshot: the README warns that PDB seqres and the PDB mmCIF files must be from exactly the same date or template search for multimers can fail, and prediction uses a max_template_date cutoff given on the command line. A result should therefore name the parameter tar, the model preset, the number of seeds per model and the template date.

sections.title: When to prefer it
sections.body: The developers give a rule. The v2.3.0 multimer models are expected to be preferred whenever the stoichiometry of the complex is known, including for structures known to be monomeric. Where the stoichiometry is unknown, for instance in genome-scale prediction, single chain AlphaFold is likely to be more accurate on average, unless the chain runs to several thousand residues. For very large or difficult targets they suggest raising the number of seeds per model to 20, which is not the default because of the cost.

quotes.text:
we expect these new models to be the preferred models whenever the
stoichiometry of the complex is known, including known monomeric structures.

In
cases where the stoichiometry is unknown, such as in genome-scale prediction, it
is likely that single chain AlphaFold will be more accurate on average unless
the chain has several thousand residues.

Increasing the number of seeds to 20
is recommended for very large or difficult targets but is not the default due to
increased computational time.

facts.value: Not stated in the repository, the v2.3.0 technical note or the configuration. These name five multimer parameter sets and the tar file that holds them but give no parameter count for the network. The AlphaFold-Multimer paper was not read, so a published count may exist there.

facts.label: Training data
facts.value: PDB structures released before 2021-09-30 for the current v2.3.0 multimer weights, about 30 per cent more data than the previous 2018-04-30 cutoff, including four times as many electron microscopy structures and twice as many structures over 2,000 residues. Training also used a self-distillation set from clustered MGnify, filtered to clusters with more than 2 sequences.

quotes.text: a new training cutoff of 2021-09-30

The new training cutoff represents ~30%
more data to train AlphaFold and more importantly includes much more data on
large protein complexes. The new training cutoff includes 4× the number of
electron microscopy structures and in aggregate twice the number of large
structures (more than 2,000 residues)

The original AF-Multimer self-distillation set
was created using the clustered MGnify dataset filtered to clusters with more
than 10 sequences.

run_guide.summary: Download the databases and parameters, then fold a multi-chain FASTA file with the multimer preset through the provided Docker script.
prerequisites: A Linux machine: the README states AlphaFold does not support other systems.
A GPU and plenty of memory: the developers' reference machine had 12 vCPUs, 85 GB of RAM and an A100.
About 3 TB of disk for the genetic databases, and aria2c installed for the download step.
Apache-2.0 for the code and CC BY 4.0 for the parameters.

notes: The record is for AlphaFold-Multimer as one of the folding models in the POISK benchmark (existing source poisk-20261115-source-manuscript-v1). There is no separate repository or model hub entry: the multimer system is a model preset of google-deepmind/alphafold, and the parameters sit in the same tar as the monomer and pTM weights. The AlphaFold-Multimer paper is only openly available as a bioRxiv preprint, which was not fetched because bioRxiv is rate-limiting this address, so coverage is marked limited. Statements about the current weights come from the repository's own v2.3.0 technical note, which describes a refit of the paper's architecture rather than a new model. Do not confuse this record with AlphaFold 3, which is a different repository with different terms.
